from pysat.solvers import Glucose3
from itertools import combinations

n = 9
edges = list(combinations(range(n), 2))
edge_idx = {e: i+1 for i, e in enumerate(edges)}  # 1-indexed

def var(i, j):
    if i > j: i, j = j, i
    return edge_idx[(i, j)]

solver = Glucose3()

# No red K_4: for every 4-subset, at least one edge must be blue (var=1 means blue)
for quad in combinations(range(n), 4):
    clause = [var(i, j) for i, j in combinations(quad, 2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)

# No blue K_3: for every 3-subset, at least one edge must be red (not blue)
for tri in combinations(range(n), 3):
    clause = [-var(i, j) for i, j in combinations(tri, 2)]
    solver.add_clause(clause)

print("SAT?", solver.solve())
